hook.text: A plant makes luxury watches and cheap toys on the same line. Neither product gets the attention it needs.

buildup.text: Focused operations dedicate resources to a narrow range of products, markets, or objectives.

discovery.text: Skinner's focused factory concept: a plant that focuses on a limited task outperforms one trying to do everything.

twist.text: Focus feels limiting, but it removes compromises that come from serving conflicting demands with shared resources.

climax.text: In-N-Out Burger's tiny menu lets it perfect every item. The focus drives quality, speed, and loyal customers.

punchline.text: Do less, better. Focus is a strategy, not a limit.

quiz.question: Why do focused operations outperform unfocused ones?
options: They eliminate compromises from conflicting demands
